title: Establish the consumer contract before writing a failing regression
applies_when: A candidate alleges a formatting, validation, shape or backend-support mismatch from a helper name or partial source window, and proposes expected behavior without tracing the producer and consumer.
lesson: Trace actual allocation/production, transformations and consumption before choosing expected behavior. DNS-SD instance labels allow punctuation that hostnames do not; applying hostname rules to every label can manufacture a failing test. Likewise, QSA speculative capture creates one metadata row per token, so replay's row count equals captured token capacity, not request count. A test that fabricates inconsistent internal metadata does not establish a reachable defect. Removing a device assertion or changing its error wording also does not establish backend support: require a documented supported caller and native kernel execution with checked outputs. Seek an observable consumer failure before repairing environments or publishing a correction.
avoid_when: Do not dismiss reachable malformed host targets, escaping/length violations, or supported callers that mutate shapes or exceed allocation capacity. Error wording may itself be a documented API contract; validate that narrower claim separately rather than inferring backend support. Static review disproves only the specific alleged mismatch; it is not a native execution test or proof of general correctness.

evidence.note: DNS-SD instance labels permit non-control punctuation and are limited to 63 octets; this is a protocol requirement, not a measured application result.
The standard explicitly distinguishes service instance names from hostnames and their naming restrictions.

One normalizer feeds both a host label and a generated service instance. A trailing hyphen in the latter alone does not establish the claimed invalid zone. Explicit overrides and native resolver behavior require separate evidence.

Speculative capture sets metadata_rows=num_tokens and slices sequence_lengths to that capacity; replay retrieves the captured metadata and derives num_rows from sequence_lengths.numel(). This counters the claim that _stage_extend_lens receives request count instead of captured token capacity for a valid initialized capture. No GPU validation is implied.

The wrapper's device assertions precede a Triton kernel launch. A CPU/meta test that only checks rejection wording does not reach that launch or validate cache writes on another accelerator. This supports a test-scope caution, not a verdict that another backend is unsupported.
